items.title: Scott Yanow interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021

ctx.x: Yeah, that’s an interesting statement and it’s fascinating to me how many stylistic changes there have been in a hundred years, and I guess if jazz started about the same time, congealed as a music when recording started, which was very fortuitous for it.

Yeah it’s a tricky thing. I mean the evolution of jazz on record is really fascinating from the 1917 to the late 70s and maybe early 80s, it’s just like a constant race towards freedom. You know each style is a little freer than the one before and — but it got to the point where okay you’ve got Cecil Taylor and how do you get freer than that? So then from that point on musicians had to use aspects of the past along with their own personality and their own ideas, combine things together. And it’s made it difficult…
Yeah. You have to — it makes it harder for you to put a label on it I guess.
